concepts.title: Hardy-Ramanujan Numbers
concepts.definition: Counting numbers that can be built by adding two cubes in more than one way (1729 = 1^3 + 12^3 = 9^3 + 10^3).
concepts.key_idea: The smallest such value is 1729 -- two different cube pairings.

solution_steps.action: identify pair of cubes for first representation
solution_steps.explain: express the number as the sum of a first pair of cubed integers

solution_steps.action: identify pair of cubes for second representation
solution_steps.explain: express the same number as the sum of a second distinct pair of cubed integers

concepts.title: Cube of a Number
concepts.definition: Take a counting number, multiply it by itself, then by itself once more.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying a quantity thrice by itself generates its third power or perfect cube.
question_patterns: find the cube of a number
calculate the cube of n
what is the cube of n
compute n cubed

solution_steps.action: multiply number by itself three times
solution_steps.explain: compute n raised to the third power

concepts.title: Difference of Consecutive Cubes Pattern
concepts.definition: An algebraic pattern where the difference between cubes of two consecutive integers equals one plus three times their product.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting successive cubes follows the expansion 1 + 3 * n * (n - 1).
question_patterns: find the value of n^3 - (n-1)^3 using pattern

Use the pattern to find 9^3 - 8^3.

solution_steps.explain: subtract 1 from the larger integer n

concepts.title: Testing Perfect Cube via Prime Factorisation
concepts.definition: A perfect cube has every prime in its factorisation showing up a multiple of three times.
concepts.key_idea: Group the primes in threes; a complete grouping means a perfect cube.
question_patterns: check whether a number is a perfect cube
is n a perfect cube
test if a given number is a perfect cube using prime factorisation
determine if n is a cube number
Is 216 a perfect cube? Break it into primes.

solution_steps.explain: deconstruct the given integer into its prime components
verify if every prime factor occurs in multiples of three
if any factor remains ungrouped into a triplet, the number is not a perfect cube

concepts.title: Smallest Multiplier to Form a Perfect Cube
concepts.definition: The smallest positive integer needed to multiply a given number so that all prime factors form complete triplets.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply by the missing factors required to complete incomplete prime factor triplets.
question_patterns: find the smallest number by which n must be multiplied to make it a perfect cube
what smallest number should be multiplied to get a perfect cube
calculate the multiplier to make n a perfect cube
by what smallest natural number must n be multiplied
What multiplies 48 to make a perfect cube?

solution_steps.action: calculate missing factor count to complete triplet
solution_steps.explain: subtract the present count of prime factor from 3
raise the incomplete prime factor to the missing count power
multiply original number by the computed multiplier

concepts.title: Smallest Divisor to Form a Perfect Cube
concepts.definition: The smallest whole number to divide out so the leftover primes group in complete threes.
concepts.key_idea: Divide by the product of prime factors that fail to form complete triplets.
question_patterns: find the smallest number by which n must be divided to obtain a perfect cube
what smallest number should n be divided by to get a perfect cube
calculate the divisor to make n a perfect cube
by what smallest natural number should n be divided
What divides 135 to leave a perfect cube?

solution_steps.action: compute divisor from leftover prime factors
solution_steps.explain: multiply prime factors that do not form triplets
divide original number by computed divisor

concepts.title: Number of Cuboids to Form a Cube
concepts.definition: The total number of identical cuboids required to build a larger cube by making all prime factors of the cuboid volume appear in triplets.
concepts.key_idea: Determine additional prime factors required to turn a cuboid's volume into a perfect cube volume.
question_patterns: how many cuboids are needed to form a cube

calculate how many cuboids of dimensions length x breadth x height make a cube
how many such cuboids will be needed to form a cube
How many 3x2x1 cuboids build a cube?

solution_steps.explain: cube the side length needed to make triplets
divide total target volume by individual cuboid volume

concepts.title: Cube Root by Prime Factorisation
concepts.definition: Determining the single number whose third power equals the given value by selecting one prime factor from each triplet group.
concepts.key_idea: Extract one representative prime factor from every triplet group and multiply them.
question_patterns: find the cube root of n by prime factorisation

solution_steps.action: take one representative factor from first triplet
solution_steps.explain: identify first prime factor group triplet

solution_steps.action: take representative factor from second triplet and multiply
solution_steps.explain: multiply representative factors from all triplets
